name: UKU Cafe
why_it_matters: The only stand-alone cafe in Khonoma listed on Tripadvisor — Khonoma's dining infrastructure is otherwise homestay kitchens. Located in the Merhuma Khel (one of the village's three khels). Tripadvisor's 'Travelers' Choice' marker sits on it though review count is low; The Better India and Nexplore Travel both cite UKU specifically as the village's cafe stop for noodles and tea.
insider_tip: Hours are unpredictable — call ahead through your homestay host or the village tourism committee. Best for a tea-and-noodles break between the heritage walk and the rice terraces; full meals are still better at your homestay.

name: Dovipie Inn Kitchen
signature_dish: Angami-style smoked pork with bamboo shoot
why_it_matters: Khonoma's only proper inn (the Tourist Lodge equivalent) — most-cited dining stop in the village beyond homestays. Tripadvisor 4.4/5 across 163 reviews. Dovipie's kitchen serves Angami-Naga homestyle dishes — pork curry with fermented bamboo shoots, fish chutney, wild apple juice, homemade aubergine pickle. Reviews flag the menu as 'limited' — that's the whole point: 4-5 honest dishes, not a multi-cuisine card.
insider_tip: Order meals at check-in or one hour ahead — kitchen is single-cook, no walk-in service. Rooms ~₹800/night with shared bathrooms; ask Apenyu (the host family) for the wild-apple drink in season (Sep-Nov).

name: Happy Hues Homestay Kitchen (Apeno's)
why_it_matters: Run by Vikepeno and Apeno Pier — Apeno is the cook, recurring across Tripadvisor and Homestays of India reviews as the headline reason guests rebook. Vegetables come from the family's terrace fields, rice from their own paddy. Naga thali, smoked pork, axone-cooked greens — village-kitchen scale, but the most consistent food story in any Khonoma homestay write-up.
insider_tip: Walk-ins occasionally accepted for lunch if you call ahead through the homestay number — the Piers also host longer stays. Apeno is a willing teacher; ask her to walk you through the axone fermentation jars, then order whatever's been simmering longest.
